# ADR 0002 — The squash commit names no agent

- **Status**: accepted
- **Scope**: `@putnami/sdd` (`agent-attribution-validate`, a step of
  `validate-workspace`), and every workspace that sets
  `options.sdd.agentAttribution`

## Context

A pull request merges by squash, and the squash commit is the only commit of
the change that reaches the base branch. Its message is the pull request title
and, when the repository squashes with it, the pull request body.

A coding agent, or the service that hosts it, can sign that message: a
"Generated by" footer, a `Co-Authored-By` trailer for a model, a link to the
agent's session. The agent's own settings do not cover every writer. A hosted
service that opens the pull request for the agent writes its own footer, and
an agent session that does not read the repository's settings writes its own
trailer. Once the commit is on the base branch, only a history rewrite removes
the signature, and a rewrite changes the ID of every later commit.

Some workspaces want no such signature in their history. Others want one. The
choice belongs to the workspace.

## Decision

1. **A step of `validate-workspace` reads the squash message.** Every gate
   that runs `validate` runs it, on any runner, as it runs the breaking-marker
   step ([ADR 0001](0001-the-squash-commit-keeps-the-breaking-marker.md)).
2. **The workspace opts in.** `options.sdd.agentAttribution` is `"allow"` or
   `"forbid"`. Unset reads as `"allow"`, and the step then passes with a note
   that says how to opt in. Any other value fails, so a typo does not turn the
   gate off.
3. **The message comes from `PUTNAMI_PROPOSAL_MESSAGE`.** It is the variable
   the breaking-marker step reads, set by the runner the same way. An unset or
   blank variable passes with a note.
4. **Three forms fail, line by line.** "Generated by" or "Generated with"
   followed by an agent's name; a `Co-Authored-By` trailer whose name or
   address is an agent's; a link to an agent's session, or the trailer that
   carries one. The agent names are one list in the engine, matched as whole
   words regardless of case. A failure names each line by its number and its
   form.
5. **Technical text passes.** A path such as `.claude/` or `.agents/`, a
   human co-author, and a generator that is not an agent are not signatures.
   A workspace that forbids attribution can still say that it is built with
   agents.
6. **The commits of the branch are not read.** They never reach the base
   branch.
7. **The step is never served from cache.** Its verdict reads an environment
   variable that the candidate cut does not hold.

## Consequences

- A pull request whose title or body names an agent fails the gate in a
  workspace that forbids it, on every runner that sets the variable.
- An edit of the title or the body is checked at the next run of the gate. A
  runner that does not run the gate on such an edit leaves the edit unchecked
  until the next push.
- The step checks the default squash message only. A person who rewrites the
  message in the merge dialog can still add a signature.
- The list of agent names is closed. A new agent host is added to it in a
  release of `@putnami/sdd`.
- A generator that shares its name with an agent, written right after
  "generated by", fails. The remedy is to reword the line.
